subject: Declared admission inputs in native project cache identity
claim: The pending native project cache-key change hashes declared source-input-lock, source-profile and target-descriptor contents and retains them for stale-request checks. The existing project-object checkpoint test has a focused selector with 21 cases passing on Windows and Debian, including the unchanged source-only key framing. This enables safe identity for later authenticated-project caching; it does not add authenticated compiler construction or complete repository source migration.

source.value: Base commit 992ba7bbebbbf3356966bdcc0ea1d2b0e5923720 plus the exact uncommitted cache implementation and test identities below. The previously tested package migration remains uncommitted and was not reverified in this run.

runs.target: Same cache code and independent temporary test inputs

limitations: The 21 cases comprise one stable complete-input request; three independent byte-mutation/key-change/stale-request/restore cases; fifteen missing, escaping, repeated, malformed and wrong-extension declarations across the three input kinds; one linked-directory rejection; and one source-only compatibility/unreferenced-input exclusion case.

Input byte hashing is not semantic admission. Native admission still owns exact source-lock digest, profile, target format, source scope and capability validation. Test admission files deliberately contain opaque bytes rather than valid production artifacts.

No source edition, compiler semantics, generated native product or installed identity was changed or qualified. The full existing cache creation/corruption/race/session test was not run; this selector exercises the changed input-identity contract only and also runs before that test in its ordinary mode.

The change-aware plan was inspected but not executed: it proposed 3410 expected seconds, including broad OS/database work and pending package changes. The focused cross-host cache checks and documentation checks remain within the ten-minute local budget.

The recalculated current split-compiler key is 0573e8aec29dbd22447cdfc664e78654e401a1a96062cc2f961b096c5c886eed and has no existing checkpoint. No cold compiler reconstruction was started; the earlier approximately 18-minute preparation is not a measured estimate for this changed state.
No peak-memory measurement, independent human review, full bootstrap convergence, repository-wide source conversion or final migration commit is claimed.
